questions.skill: Explain and construct extraneous solutions
questions.standard_level: Algebra II. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra II, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Solving x/(x - 2) + 1 = 2/(x - 2), Leo multiplies both sides by x - 2 and gets x = 2. Why is x = 2 extraneous?
questions.prompt_markup: Solving x/(x - 2) + 1 = 2/(x - 2), Leo multiplies both sides by x - 2 and gets x = 2. Why is x = 2 extraneous?

choices.text: x = 2 is extraneous because it is positive, and solutions of rational equations must be negative.
x = 2 makes both sides equal after multiplying by x - 2, so it is a solution of the original equation and is not extraneous.
Leo made an arithmetic error when he multiplied; the correct solution of the equation is x = -2.
Multiplying by x - 2 is not reversible when x - 2 = 0, so the new equation can be true at x = 2 even though the original equation is undefined there.

questions.correct_answer: Multiplying by x - 2 is not reversible when x - 2 = 0, so the new equation can be true at x = 2 even though the original equation is undefined there.
questions.grading_note: At x = 2 the original denominators are 0. The others give irrelevant reasons, invent another solution (x = -2 gives -2/(-4) + 1 = 1/2 ≠ -1/2), or ignore the undefined denominators.

questions.skill: See rational equations as graph intersections
questions.standard_level: Algebra II. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra II, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Why does x/(x - 2) + 1 = 2/(x - 2) have no solution, in terms of the graphs of y = x/(x - 2) + 1 and y = 2/(x - 2)?
questions.prompt_markup: Why does x/(x - 2) + 1 = 2/(x - 2) have no solution, in terms of the graphs of y = x/(x - 2) + 1 and y = 2/(x - 2)?

choices.text: For x ≠ 2 the left side minus the right side is (2x - 4)/(x - 2) = 2, so the graphs never meet.
The graphs meet at x = 2, where both expressions have the same value, so x = 2 is a solution.
The two graphs are the same curve, so every x except 2 is a solution of the equation.
The graphs cross at x = 0 and nowhere else, so x = 0 is the only solution of the equation.

questions.correct_answer: For x ≠ 2 the left side minus the right side is (2x - 4)/(x - 2) = 2, so the graphs never meet.
questions.grading_note: The difference of the two functions is the constant 2 on their common domain. The others use the excluded x = 2 or false claims (at x = 0 the sides are 1 and -1).
